Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, bandwidth-bound decoding latency is governed by how well the attention kernel can keep the memory subsystem saturated while hiding latency. Unified memory, L1/L2 caches, shared memory, and LPDDR5X each change the effective bandwidth and latency profile, but the dominant factor in hybrid/full-attention LLMs is the ability to stream KV-cache and input tokens at the memory bandwidth limit without stalling on cache misses or PCIe/DDR traffic.

Here’s a self-contained Python implementation of a bounded lock-free-style ring buffer simulator with producer/consumer backpressure metrics and unit tests.

Notes:
- “Lock-free style” here means:
  - Single-producer / single-consumer (SPSC) to keep it simple and correct without complex CAS loops.
  - Uses a single atomic head/tail with modulo indexing.
  - No Python-level locks; concurrency is simulated via a scheduler.
- Backpressure metrics:
  - Producer: number of times it was blocked because the buffer was full.
  - Consumer: number of times it was blocked
